tasks.title: Mars
tasks.reason: Each process call receives only a local 3x3 array and must return a 100-bit state; globals and out-of-band process communication are forbidden. The sole persistent information channel is returned cell memory.

tasks.title: Magic Show
tasks.reason: Alice chooses a tree encoding X after setN; Bob receives only the surviving edges after deletions and must recover X. Separate encoder/decoder communication, not a hidden-state search oracle.

tasks.title: Hack!
tasks.reason: hack() must recover hidden bucket count n by calling collisions(x); each call returns feedback and consumes total vector-length budget. This is interactive despite an absent list badge.

tasks.title: Permutation Game
tasks.reason: Alice submits selected permutation indices to Bob(t); the grader chooses and returns an edge, changing the permutation. The strategy must handle arbitrary opponent responses. No separate encoding/decoding channel.

tasks.title: Navigation
tasks.reason: construct_network assigns cable types with full tree knowledge; navigate runs in a separate process and sees only local types, K and B. Calls may be reordered, so the encoded edge labels carry the information.

tasks.title: Scallion Pancake Party
tasks.reason: Each guest process knows only its forbidden flavor and optional room index, then changes slice counts through strategy; a separate final guess process reconstructs the permutation from surviving bags. Communication through constrained shared objects.

tasks.title: Game
tasks.reason: init supplies n/k and add_teleporter supplies each new edge; the contestant returns cycle detection results. An online input API does not request hidden grader information.

tasks.title: September
tasks.reason: solve receives the complete tree and every volunteer sequence, then returns one maximum day count.

tasks.title: Train
tasks.reason: solve receives the entire timetable, costs and meal intervals, then returns the minimum cost.

tasks.title: Rotating Lines
tasks.reason: energy receives all angles; rotate(t,x) returns void and only applies known deterministic changes. No hidden-information feedback or separate receiver.

tasks.title: APIOBike
tasks.reason: Full tree and both bike count arrays are provided; return route and delivery arrays. No oracle or separate receiver.

tasks.title: Cyberland
tasks.reason: solve receives the complete road graph, country abilities and halving limit, then returns one minimum travel time; no hidden-information query or separate receiver.

tasks.title: Alice, Bob, and Circuit
tasks.reason: Alice encodes member names/numbers and Bob independently encodes letter endpoints into bounded bitstrings. Circuit sees only their lengths when constructing a Boolean circuit that decodes result sums; no party has all input and there is no adaptive query oracle.
tasks.provenance: APIO2023 organizer public repository, pinned commit

tasks.title: Sequence
tasks.reason: sequence receives the full array and returns one maximum median-frequency count. No hidden-information query or encoded message for a separate receiver.
tasks.provenance: APIO2023 organizer public repository, pinned commit

tasks.title: Permutation
tasks.reason: construct_permutation receives the desired subsequence count k and returns a permutation; each supplied k is an independent scenario, not a hidden-state or communication task.
